For the regularized comparison functions \(V_\varepsilon=(|f|^2+\eta|z|^2+\varepsilon)^{1/2}\) and \(U_\varepsilon=(|h|^2+|g|^2+\eta|z|^2+\varepsilon)^{1/2}\), direct differentiation gives the stated lower and upper Laplacian estimates. Because \(V_\varepsilon^2\le2U_\varepsilon^2\), Green's mean identity and \(g(0)=0\) give the uniform radial \(H^1\) estimate; letting \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\) is legitimate at each fixed radius. The Poisson-kernel example correctly shows that arbitrary harmonic \(\mathbf h^1\) need not split into \(H^1\) components.
